title: stabilize-sse-boundary-coalescer-and-call-sentinel-ordering
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: We continue to see rare production cases where SSE stream coalescing merges delimiter bytes across chunk boundaries or reorders function-call sentinels when the upstream chunker emits tightly-coupled events. The symptom is intermittent 'partial JSON' errors at the client (OpenAI-compat consumers) and tool/function-call payloads being split or reordered under high concurrency. This PR introduces a conservative coalescer and ordering watermark to eliminate delimiter leakage and to guarantee event-level ordering for call sentinels without materially regressing throughput.

Summary of changes (high level): added a sentinel-aware coalescer state machine in the streaming layer (pkg/stream/coalescer.go), introduced a sequence-watermark header (sse-seq) that is attached to emitted events, updated the OpenAI-compat parser to prefer last-complete-JSON with the new watermark heuristic, and added deterministic function-call boundary tests and fuzz harnesses. Also added a short-lived canary flag and a 5% traffic rollout plan in the console routing code (internal/routing/canary.go).

Why this is different from prior fixes: previous PRs focused on reassembly heuristics in the parser. This change stops the delimiter leakage earlier by making the coalescer aware of sentinels and by introducing an emission hysteresis that defers emission of ambiguous trailing bytes until the next chunk arrives or the watermark advances. That prevents two classes of failures: (1) trailing delimiter becoming the prefix of the next event, and (2) function-call sentinel bytes being split across a flush boundary and then reassembled out-of-order by concurrent handlers.

Checklist: - [x] Add coalescer state machine with unit tests - [x] Add watermark header and wire to router/emit path - [x] Backwards-compatible parser change with graceful fallback to old behavior when watermark absent - [x] Add deterministic and fuzz tests for partial JSON cases - [x] Performance microbench and 95th latency regression check (<= 6% overhead at 512 concurrent streams) - [x] Canary rollout plan documented in PR notes

Testing: Unit tests cover coalescer transitions, watermark increments, and parser compatibility. Integration e2e streaming tests added using the existing redwood-openai-compat harness to simulate interleaved sentinel emission and mid-chunk splits. A small fuzz harness (tests/stream/fuzz_partial_json_test.go) reproduces previously-observed crash traces. CI flakiness was addressed by increasing the deterministic seed for buffered flush timings. Perf benches show a small CPU overhead (~4%) under synthetic worst-case microbench; production telemetry will be used to validate real workload impact.

Deployment and rollback: The change is gated behind a feature flag (stream.coalescer_v2) for the first rollout. Console routing allows enabling for a customer or a percentage. Rollout plan: enable 5% of traffic for 24h (canary), monitor streaming error rate and function-call misordering rate, then 25% for 6h, and finally 100% if no regressions. Rollback is a single-toggle to revert to the previous coalescer; the parser still accepts streams without sse-seq to preserve interop.

Risk and mitigations: The main risk is an unanticipated throughput regression under highly bursty small-chunk workloads. Mitigations: conservative emission hysteresis default window (2ms), auto-disable on observed latency SLO breach, and telemetry counters for coalescer-hits/misses. The watermark header is optional (backwards-compatible) so old clients won't be affected.

Related: SUP-8124 contains the customer incident that motivated this change; ENG-2435 tracks the long-term streaming resiliency work.

Release notes: Stabilize SSE streaming coalescing and function-call ordering to avoid partial-JSON consumer errors and sentinel misordering. Backwards compatible; enabled behind feature flag.

review_conversation: Ava Patel (reviewer): Found a race in the coalescer state transition where pending trailing bytes could be dropped when a timeout triggers. Requested an explicit pending-buffer drain in the abort path. (addressed)
Author (Jordan Kim): Added explicit drain and updated coalescer_test to cover the timeout abort case. Also added comment describing the hysteresis tradeoff.
Diego Morales (reviewer): Please add a perf microbenchmark and quantify latency/regression before merge. Also asked for a canary plan to be included in release notes. (addressed)
Linus Schneider (approver): Verified e2e tests locally; requested increasing fuzz iterations from 100 to 1000 for a couple of seeds. After that, approved with minor nits.
CI: initial e2e streaming job flaked on a timing-dependent test; test was stabilized and re-run. All checks passed on rerun.
release_notes: Fix: stabilize SSE coalescing to prevent partial-JSON emits and ensure function-call sentinel ordering. Backwards compatible; default gated behind feature flag stream.coalescer_v2. See console docs for canary rollout steps.
merge_outcome: merged successfully with squash; post-merge actions: monitor streaming.errors and sse.coalescer_hysteresis_counters, schedule follow-up ENG-2491 to refine hysteresis defaults based on production telemetry
